newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan hopes for three rounds of summer Cyprus talks.
newsitem.headline: Annan hopes for three rounds of summer Cyprus talks.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Tuesday that if a face-to-face meeting in June between the leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities went well, he hoped to hold two more sessions that would provide an indication by September whether progress could be made.

"I do hope that the two leaders will come prepared to work with me to resolve this long-standing conflict," he said, replying to a question from a Cyprus Broadcasting Corporation reporter during a global forum organised by the CNN cable news network.

Cyprus has been virtually partitioned since 1974 when troops from Turkey took over the north of the island after a brief coup in Nicosia engineered by the junta then ruling Greece. The United Nations has been trying for more than 20 years to reunite Cyprus under a federal system.
Annan, who was visiting Atlanta, Georgia, said he had met both President Glafcos Clerides, head of the Greek Cypriot community, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.
The secretary-general added: "If all goes well, in June I would expect to have a face-to-face meeting. We would invite the two leaders. I would open the meeting."

If he could not be present, the talks would be chaired by his recently appointed special adviser, Diego Cordovez, a former Ecuadorean foreign minister who, as a U.N. under-secretary-general, headed negotiations on Afghanistan in the late 1980s.

"If the June talks go well, we would hope to have two more sessions and hopefully have a clear indication by August or September whether we are going to make real progress or not...So we will, at maximum, have three sessions this summer, if all goes well."
Although Annan did not say so, it would be difficult to continue negotiations during the run-up to elections that the Greek Cypriots are scheduled to hold next February.

U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhart told reporters in New York that representatives of the five permanent members of the Security Council -- the United States, Russia, Britain, France and China -- were meeting later at U.N. headquarters to discuss the Cyprus problem.

"I understand that there is at least one paper circulating at that meeting. But it is not a United Nations proposal, it is from one of the permanent members," he said, without identifying the author of the paper.
He said Annan "feels that the situation in Cyprus has deteriorated and that any effort that could help improve the atmospherics there would be a plus. That is his minimal objective for this year."
The top U.N. officials involved in the Cyprus question conferred at the United Nations on Tuesday and would join the meeting of the five permanent council members later, he added.

In addition to Cordovez, the officials are: Gustave Feissel, the U.N.'s resident representative in Cyprus; U.N. special representative Han Sung-Joo of South Korea, who is retiring from that post at the end of this month; and the under-secretary-general for political affairs, Sir Kiernan Prendergast.
